execution.description: Diagnosed and fixed the worker-images-v2 PyTorch GPU rebuild of fno_defaults, which failed both repeats after about 640 s with a one-device error while the MLP rebuilt bit-identically 4 of 4.

expected: Moving a family's module to the device (Module.to) before each call places everything it computes with on that device, so a recipe trained on CUDA predicts on the CPU like any other.
observed: neuraloperator's grid embedding caches its positional grid as a plain attribute on the first call and reuses it whatever device a later call asks for. Module.to moves parameters and buffers only. Training on CUDA cached a CUDA grid; prediction then ran on the CPU and concatenated CPU features with it. CPU-only tests could never see this, because every call ran on one device.
keep: Every PyTorch family's library modules are placed on the call's device by one shared path (torch_training.follow_device), including tensors a library caches as plain attributes.
A device-parity test calls every family on the CPU and then on a second device (CUDA, else meta) and asserts every held tensor and output follows; it reproduces this failure without a GPU.
change: Test any new PyTorch family, or any new library version, with the cross-device parity test before it reaches a GPU image.
Run the cross-device round trip (CUDA training, CPU prediction) on the GPU lane for every family before a GPU image is released.
